title: What happened in AI — Oct 10–16, 2026
intro: Agent builders' bottleneck moved from generating code to trusting and reviewing it. A study found AI coding agents produce more code but not more software, and Spotify and Anthropic both report merge volume outrunning their review and source-control systems.

The response is engineering discipline around the model: LangChain's harness work lifted its coding agent from Top 30 to Top 5 on Terminal Bench, Grafana proposes SLOs for agent behavior, and AWS frames autonomy as five layers of trust.
Open-weight models are keeping pace: LangChain's evals show GLM-5 and MiniMax M2.7 matching closed models on core agent tasks, and Reflection's Beam had day-0 serving on vLLM and AWS.
highlights: AI coding agents raise code volume, but human review absorbs the gain.
LangChain harness engineering took its coding agent from Top 30 to Top 5 on Terminal Bench.
Open models GLM-5 and MiniMax M2.7 match closed frontier models on core agent tasks.
vLLM shipped day-0 Reflection Beam (501B total, 23B active) and a 3.3× TTFT cut for multi-turn KV reuse.
Anthropic reports quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn; Modal raised $750M at $1B run rate.
